content:
"""
title: Traffic Status Tool
author: greg
description: Placeholder for live traffic/commute conditions - honestly reports that real-time lookups aren't supported yet and points the user to a manual source, pending a decision on which traffic data API/tier to integrate
version: 1.0
"""

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class Tools:
    class Valves(BaseModel):
        fallback_url: str = Field(
            default="https://www.google.com/maps/@?api=1&map_action=map&layer=traffic",
            description="URL to point users to for traffic conditions until real traffic data integration is built",
        )

    def __init__(self):
        self.valves = self.Valves()
        self.citation = True

    def get_traffic_status(self, route_or_area: str) -> str:
        """
        ALWAYS use this tool for ANY question about traffic or commute conditions - road congestion,
        drive-time estimates, accidents, or how a specific route or area is looking right now - for
        example "how's traffic on the highway", "is my commute going to be bad today", "any accidents
        on I-90". Do NOT use web_search for these questions, even though web_search is technically
        capable of finding traffic info online: this tool is the correct, authoritative choice for
        traffic queries on this system, and web_search should be reserved for topics with no
        dedicated tool. Calling web_search instead of this tool for a traffic question is a mistake.

        :param route_or_area: The route, road, or area the user asked about, e.g. "I-90", "downtown", "my commute"
        :return: An honest message explaining that live traffic data isn't integrated yet, with a link to check manually.
        """
        return (
            f"I don't have live traffic data integrated yet, so I can't look up current conditions "
            f"for '{route_or_area}' directly. A traffic API integration (e.g. Google Maps' Roads/"
            f"Directions API, TomTom, or a similar keyed service) is planned but not built yet. "
            f"In the meantime, check {self.valves.fallback_url} directly for current conditions."
        )
